sentence: Liver blood tests point towards a possible problem but cannot name the cause, and abnormal results are common and often not serious.
note: LTO: abnormal tests point to further investigation but do not diagnose a cause; BLT: abnormal common

sentence: Liver blood tests are a group of blood tests, once known as liver function tests or LFTs.
note: BLT page title: liver blood tests (formerly LFTs)

sentence: They usually include ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, bilirubin and albumin.
They are often done as routine tests, so abnormal results are sometimes found by chance when blood is taken for another reason.
ALT and AST are enzymes that leak into the blood when liver cells are injured.
note: blended summary: ALT/AST reflect liver cell injury; the enzyme wording is textbook

sentence: ALT is more specific to the liver, while AST can also be high when muscle is damaged elsewhere in the body.
Common causes of this pattern include viral hepatitis, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, autoimmune hepatitis and drug-induced liver injury.
Raised ALP and GGT point towards a problem with the flow of bile.
note: pathway: predominantly raised ALP and GGT indicate cholestasis

sentence: Causes include blocked bile ducts, for example by stones, and some long-term diseases of the bile ducts.
ALP also comes from bone, so GGT helps to show whether the liver is the source.
Raised bilirubin causes jaundice, a yellowing of the eyes and skin.
Bilirubin can also be raised without liver disease, as in Gilbert's syndrome, where the other liver tests are normal.
Albumin is affected only when liver disease is at a severe stage, and low albumin also has other causes such as malnutrition, kidney protein loss and inflammation.
Abnormal results can occur in conditions that do not involve the liver, and normal results can be found in people with serious liver disease.
The British Liver Trust says it is quite common to get a result that is not normal, and this does not always mean a liver condition.
It adds that the liver can take a lot of damage before it causes problems, so a normal result is a good sign but not a guarantee.
Illness, shock, burns, injury, severe exercise, pregnancy and a reaction to medicines can all change one or more of the tests.
Sometimes a repeat test is all that is needed.
Laboratories compare each result with their own range, so results are compared only with the range of the laboratory that did the test.
If the results suggest a liver problem, a GP may calculate a FIB-4 index, which gives an indication of the amount of scarring in the liver.
People at high risk of liver disease, or with symptoms, are referred or have more tests.
Further tests can look for the cause, such as viral hepatitis, fatty liver disease or an effect of alcohol or medicines.
The NHS says jaundice can be a sign of something serious such as liver disease.
It advises asking for an urgent GP appointment or contacting NHS 111 when the skin or whites of the eyes look yellow.
On brown or black skin the yellow colour is easier to see in the whites of the eyes.
Itchy skin, darker urine and paler stools can come with it.
Liver blood tests, once called liver function tests, are a group of tests that include ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, bilirubin and albumin.
A result outside the reference range does not always mean liver disease, and a normal result does not always rule it out.
note: LTO: abnormal results occur without liver disease and normal results occur in serious liver disease; BLT

sentence: The pattern of results helps point towards liver cell injury or a problem with bile flow.
note: LTO / City and Hackney pathway: hepatocellular vs cholestatic pattern

sentence: Yellowing of the skin or eyes needs an urgent GP appointment or a call to NHS 111, according to the NHS.
